The results of the research are an Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller can operate and be implemented, to design this prototype, easier operation, thereby reducing the potential for operational errors and avoiding the risk of injury or injury damage to equipment.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System with H2O Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: With advances in technology, future events can be predicted or categorized based on knowledge gathered in the past so that errors can be minimized. These strategies play an essential role in avoiding attacks on large-scale data network systems in more specialized technological fields, especially computer network systems. IDS (Instruction Detection System) can mitigate large-scale network system attacks by detecting suspicious behavior in network systems. The Deep Learning approach, which uses artificial neural networks, is used to help maintain network systems using IDS. In this study, researchers used the RapidMiner application program to help analyze the data set. Results obtained by using the Deep Learning H2O algorithm method with a dataset of 25192 data training and 42 records produced the highest level of accuracy and a recall value of 99.36% for ratios (number division) of 0.6 and 0.4 for epoch values of 40 activations using the rectifier itself. For wave rectifiers, or what is commonly known as input and output, these results are obtained from the model created as a system used to classify network attacks.

articleTitle: Panic Button Application for Android-Based Environmental Security Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Environmental security is currently given less attention, especially in the community environment at the RT/RW level. This is due to a lack of communication and concern among the residents themselves, either because of their extensive activities outside the home, such as working in offices, factories, or fields, or even due to seclusion within the house, resulting in limited interaction with neighbors. These conditions have led to several environmental threats, including crimes such as theft, mugging, and kidnapping; social disasters such as fires; seriously ill neighbors in need of help; and incidents of Domestic Violence (KDRT). The purpose of this research is to develop a Panic Button application that can be implemented on residents’ smartphones to provide security services for residents experiencing panic situations. The method used in this study is the Extreme Programming (XP) method with several stages: planning, design, coding, and testing. The research findings show that residents’ smartphones are used as a communication medium with Mini PCs connected to speakers in the RT/RW hall or special locations to emit warning signals (according to the occurring phenomenon). The test results show that all the features in the application have been running well; this can be proven by the results of the questionnaire, which stated that 83% of respondents stated that the functions contained in the application were running normally, and 88% of respondents stated that they strongly agreed that application features made it easier to report incidents panic in the RT/RW environment, and 75% of respondents stated that the speed of incident handling could be handled by this application. Additionally, each user (citizen) receives notifications containing the incident’s name and address. For future research, this panic button application can run on the iOS operating system.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Clustering Approach For Analyzing A Multivariate Time Series Dataset, Case Study COVID-19 Outbreak in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) became a pandemic across the world in 2020 - 2022. Indonesia is one of the countries affected by the COVID-19 outbreak. As an archipelago country, the spreading of COVID-19 in one and other provinces varies. This study is conducted to cluster the provinces in Indonesia according to the daily new cases, deaths, and recoveries of COVID-19 patients. It implements Intelligent Kernel K-Means and Intelligent K-Means to cluster multivariate time series data without determining the number of clusters. Intelligent Kernel K-Means finds two clusters and obtains the best average Silhouette score of 0.81. It also reveals that the severity of COVID-19 in some areas correlated to the variables population density, population, general hospitals, inpatient health centers, not inpatient health centers, urban areas with water pollution, urban areas with land pollution, urban areas with air pollution, and urban areas without pollution.

articleTitle: Arduino and LabVIEW Based Ping-Pong Ball Position Control using PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Industrial development requires accurate and reliable control technology. One of the popular control systems is PID control. This paper discusses the implementation of the PID method for ping-pong ball position control by utilizing the theory of the Coanda effect. The control system was designed using Arduino as the controller and LabVIEW as the control interface. Tests were carried out by combining set point values to determine whether the position control system worked properly or not. The test results show that the PID method combined with LabVIEW can work well with the results of the PID control test at successive heights of 15 cm, 20 cm, 25 cm, 30 cm, and 35 cm obtained rise time (tr) 3.49 seconds, 4.58 seconds, 9.08 sec, 9.92 sec, and 8.84 sec. The average tolerance is 1.5 cm for the upper limit and 1 cm for the lower limit.

articleTitle: Implementation of the K-Nearest Neighbors Algorithm in the AgroWeather System for Plant Recommendations Based on Weather Predictions
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This study aims to develop an accurate weather prediction model that can be applied using the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) method to make it easier for the community, especially farmers, to know the weather in the future and to match plants that must be planted in certain seasons in Bandung Regency. Rising temperatures and climate change occurring in Bandung, West Java, have a significant impact on rice cultivation and agricultural production. With reliable weather predictions, farmers can avoid the risks associated with growing crops that are not suited to the weather conditions, such as pest attacks, plant diseases, and crop failure. The KNN method is a useful approach to predicting weather conditions based on historical data. The results of this research can help farmers or agricultural experts determine suitable plants to plant based on weather forecasts. The targeted output is a weather prediction model that can be integrated into an agricultural information system in Bandung Regency. This model has an accuracy rate of 90& in providing farmers with relevant information for the coming season and updates regarding weather conditions. In addition, this model also provides plant type recommendations with an accuracy rate of 85&. These recommendations are based on an analysis of historical data on crops that have done well in each previous season.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband CPW-fed Printed Monopole Antenna for 5G and CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: An ultra-wide band (UWB) linearly polarized CPW-fed printed monopole antenna is designed. The proposed antenna has a total size of 1.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×1.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.23λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> operates in C-band, achieves a wide -10 dB impedance bandwidth and a high gain. To maintain the UWB feature and to enhance the radiation performance, the circular shaped patch, and the Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) respectively. Moreover, the multi in-phase properties of AMC’s unit cell leads to a significant increase of the total gain. The simulation results show a UWB of 193.1% (4.8-16 GHz) and a octal gain of 8.9 dBi at an operating frequency of 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis on Tourism Place using Naive Bayes
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The method of extracting information from a text is called text mining. In contrast, sentiment analysis involves examining text data to determine whether a statement expresses good or negative conversations. In this study, a system was developed that categorizes tweets about West Bandung Regency tourism spots that contain both favorable and negative remarks. The Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM) technique is used to carry out the classification process utilizing the Naive Bayes algorithm. You will learn how locals feel about West Bandung Regency’s tourist attractions through this method. Six scenarios were developed using the categorization findings from 250 pieces of data that included both positive and negative sentiment. The scenario has got the greatest f1-score of 82.8%. These findings demonstrate how effectively the Naive Bayes algorithm performs sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Forward Chaining and Certainly Factor Method Optimization for Lung Disease Expert System
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to build a system which is capable of diagnosing lung disease, to provide information about lung disease along with treatment solutions so that it can help the public, and to determine the best method to use in the system to be built. From the results of the analysis by comparing several methods that can be used in Expert Systems for diagnosing lung disease, the result is that by implementing a combination of the Forward Chaining method and the Certain Factor, the highest level of accuracy of results is obtained among other methods. After several tests using software testing, user questionnaires and expert validation, it is proved that this Expert System can assist patients in diagnosing lung disease with a diagnostic accuracy rate of 93 percent, and ready used by the public.

articleTitle: Electroencephalography (EEG) Signal Identification for Epilepsy Using Support Vector Machine (SVM)
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Epilepsy causes seizures due to abnormal brain electrical activity. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are used in many medical applications, including epileptic seizure detection since they capture brain electrical activity. Neurologists have made inferences from visual observation. However, this technique takes time and depends on the reader’s skill. Thus, epilepsy detection must be automated, and machine learning can be used. This study concerns epilepsy EEG signal identification. Classifying preictal and ictal EEG signals and assessing the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method’s accuracy, precision, recall, and error value to identify epilepsy EEG signals. SVM will identify data based on ictal labels (1.0) and preictal (0.0) in the dataset with numerous parameters and data split ratio modifications. The first experiment evaluates the c parameter with a 7:3 data split ratio and the default rbf kernel. The training and validation stages produced accuracy, precision, and sensitivity values above 95% and an error rate below 0.5%. The second experiment tests kernel parameters with a 7:3 data split ratio. The C kernel parameter is set to its default value of 1. The training and validation stages produce over 77% accuracy, precision, and sensitivity with an error rate of 1.6%. The third experiment examines how changing the training-testing data split ratio affects the default kernel and parameter c. The training and validation steps produce 77% accuracy, precision, and recall with an error rate of 1.6%. Parameters and variations split data during testing to isolate the best data using parameters and ratios.

articleTitle: A Review of Coverage Predictions in Mobile Communication Systems using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The needs for best signal coverage and high performance cellular network quality is critical in planning, designing, and operating 5G cellular networks due to the maturity of Internet penetration in today’s society. In the process of cellular network planning and optimization, accurate predictions are required. With this accurate coverage prediction, mobile network operators can identify areas that require network infrastructure improvements, as well as optimize network resources to improve the quality of service provided. There are several factors that influence coverage analysis and prediction, including the distance between the transmitter and receiver, topographic depiction of the area modeled in the propagation path loss model, weather, signal interference, and other factors. There are several methods for predicting coverage or coverage of signal power levels at the receiver. These methods have been developed in previous research including model-based prediction methods and data-driven prediction methods. Model-based prediction methods are based on empirical models of network characteristics and environmental parameters, while data-driven prediction methods are based on processing signal data and environmental data that have been collected from cellular networks and simulated using machine learning algorithms. In addition to these two methods, there are also studies that use a combination of the two methods to be used in predicting coverage or predicting other functions in cellular communication systems. This paper will present a review of research papers related to these two methods, including the development of the methods.

articleTitle: Web-based Face Detection and Recognition using YOLO and Dlib
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The electronic-based government system (SPBE) is an effort initiated by the Indonesian government to create a clean and trustworthy governance and public service system. However, the government’s public services involve sensitive data owned by Indonesian citizens. An identity verification system is needed to ensure the security and integrity of the system and prevent system abuse. A face recognition system is arguably the most accessible biometric verification method available. This paper used YOLOv5-Face and YOLOv7-Face pre-trained models for face detection. The models were then integrated with the Dlib library to identify faces based on their identities. Testing was performed by determining a confusion matrix for each weight used. The best-performing face recognition system was then implemented as a web application. The yolov7-lite-s weight achieved an accuracy of 94.5% with an average processing time of 237.45 ms per image on a private dataset.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Data Communication Architecture on Real-Time Face Recognition for Hybrid Laboratory System
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have reshaped educational technology, increasing the chances of developing more effective and engaging learning environments. This study proposes an architecture for asynchronous data communication with real-time face recognition, a virtual and remote labs confluence. The architecture uses IoT hardware and software to comprise critical components such as IoT cameras, message brokers, FTP servers, and AI processing servers. The aim is to optimize resource usage and maximize response time efficiency. The architecture employs message queuing to manage high volumes of face image data, facilitating immediate verification and rapid access. Our findings demonstrate that the system can achieve face recognition with 91.7% accuracy and an average system communication latency of 2.631 seconds, effectively leveraging asynchronous communication to optimize resource usage and computational efficiency. The research comprehensively measures the data communication metrics and face recognition metrics. It also explains how asynchronous data communication can be strategically deployed in a hybrid lab environment to enhance educational and operational efficacy.

articleTitle: Using Zero-Knowledge Proof in Privacy-Preserving Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The role of digital identity systems in today’s cyber infrastructure is pivotal to providing secure access to online services. Privacy-preserving mechanisms, however, are becoming more important as cyber threats develop. Especially in large networks, zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) are an effective way to enhance privacy in digital identity systems. When used during authentication, they protect the privacy of user data by verifying knowledge to another entity without unveiling the actual data. A ZKP can also reduce identity theft risks, mitigate man-in-the-middle attacks, and enhance security when integrated into privacy-preserving networks. In this paper, we examine the role that ZKPs play in privacy-preserving networks and the possibility of using them in this regard, in order to gain insight into their application in digital identity systems.

articleTitle: Pores Segmentation Based on Active Contour Model for Automatic Wood Species Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Wood species identification based on computer vision is an alternative solution in early-stage identification to obtain faster accuracy results. Hence, the development of computer-based identification is highly required. Each wood species has its unique anatomical characteristics. One of these characteristics is the pore. In order to obtain the pores object from the surrounding environment in a wood image, a segmentation is required. The aim of this research is to propose an automatic algorithm based on Active Contour model for wood pores segmentation in the wood species identification. In this research, three Active Contour segmentation models were used to obtain pores objects, i.e., Chan Vese (CV), Region Scalable Fitting (RSF) and Geodesic Active Contour (GAC) model. Nine commercial wood species will be used as a dataset to be segmented with different pore sizes. The result showed that the Chan Vese (CV) model is the best model for the pores segmentation than the RSF and GAC model with the highest IoU average value of 0.8883, the lowest iteration (N = 80), and the fastest segmentation running time (T) which ranges from 54.01 to 62.64 seconds.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Monitoring System of Vital Signs using IR-UWB Radar: A Short Review and Feasibility Study
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Monitoring vital signs regularly helps the early recognition of abnormal physiological parameters in deteriorating patients. Impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) technology is a suitable non-invasive approach to monitor the vital signs such as heart and breathing rates. In this technique, the IR-UWB radar antenna propagates signal towards the patient and the reflected spectrum can determine the status of the vital signs. This function is ideal where patient touching should be avoided such as a potentially infected COVID-19 patients. This paper designs an algorithm to identify the chest displacement and to separate the heart and breathing signals. In addition, we propose an adaptive filter and a smoothing filter used in the function to reduce the measurement noise from the surrounding vibrations. We have implemented the device and validated the performance over different sets of real experiments. The results show that the proposed technology can effectively estimate the breathing and heart rates with up to 98% accuracy as compared to the values obtained using an electrocardiograph (ECG).

articleTitle: Noninvasive Pathological Staging of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma using Computed Tomography-based Radiomics Features and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: According to Global Burden of Cancer data 2018, kidney cancer is one of the cancer cases that causes 9.6 million deaths in 185 countries. Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is the most common type of RCC cancer. Accurate staging of ccRCC is important for determining prognosis and formulating effective treatment. A radiomics approach is proposed as non-invasively I to IV pathological staging of ccRCC using computed tomography (CT) images. 190 patients with pathological ccRCC stages I to IV were included. The research process consists of: patient selection, cancer mask segmentation, feature extraction and selection, and classification. 33 radiomics features were selected and used for system training using support vector machine (SVM) and provided the accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of the tested dataset are 90%, 90%, and 96.67%, respectively. These results indicate that the pathological stage of ccRCC can be predicted significantly based on radiomics features on CT images. Radiomics features on 3D CT images can incredibly predict four pathological stages of ccRCC non-invasively. And machine learning can also be used to analyze potential feature sets and construct classification systems. To increase system reliability, potential directions of secured data sharing technology is also discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Innovating Scholarship Design: a Comprehensive Approach Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: In the realm of higher education, ensuring equitable access to scholarships is paramount to fostering inclusive learning environments. The traditional methods of scholarship allocation, often reliant on rigid metrics, may not always capture the diverse needs and backgrounds of prospective recipients. This paper introduces an innovative approach to scholarship design using fuzzy logic, a computational technique that provides nuanced decision-making capabilities. Through our method, scholarship eligibility is not treated as a binary, but rather a spectrum, allowing for greater consideration of various socio-economic, academic, and extracurricular factors. We employed a comprehensive fuzzy inference system to assess a broad range of applicant criteria, ensuring that the scholarship allocation process becomes both more equitable and adaptive to individual circumstances. Our results demonstrate that the fuzzy logic-based system offers a higher degree of flexibility and accuracy in scholarship distribution compared to traditional methods. With its potential to revolutionize how scholarships are granted, this approach paves the way for a more inclusive and holistic educational landscape.

articleTitle: EEG Signal Classification using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and Gaussian Support Vector Machine (SVM) for Epileptics
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: As a potentially life-threatening neurological disorder, epilepsy needs early treatment to prevent the deterioration of the patient’s condition. Electroencephalogram (EEG) technology-based detection is a recommended method for accurate diagnosis to help distinguish the state of normal patients from patients with epilepsy. In this study, EEG recording data was obtained from a database of Klinik fiir Epileptologie, University of Bonn. The data consisted of five conditions involving nono-epilepsy volunteers and patients with epilepsy engaged in different activities. Our proposed design consists of several stages, such as dataset input, decomposition, and feature extraction (including minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, and skewness), performed through Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) on wavelet coefficients and classified using Support Vector Machine (SVM). Our design involved the DWT utilizing Daubechies and Gaussian wavelet types, while SVM employed a classification approach. The system’s performance was evaluated using K-Fold cross-validation and Confusion Matrix analysis. The best accuracy results, obtained from normal patients and epileptics (Cl: ABCDE) with DWT and SVM methods, showed a maximum accuracy of 78.6%. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach in distinguishing between normal patients and those with epilepsy, indicating its significance in epilepsy diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Network Performance Measurement on Discord Server Regions with Voice Debugging
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research paper explores the quality of 4G network services provided by various cellular operators in Indonesia, including Telkomsel, ByU, IM3 Ooredo, 3, XL, LiveOn, AXIS, and Smartfren. It also examines the performance of Discord voice chat servers in Asia, specifically in Singapore, Japan, India, and Hong Kong. The study was conducted within the Discord gaming community server. The performance of service quality was evaluated using several methods: packet capturing with Wireshark for Quality of Service (QoS), Discord voice debugging, and the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) Extended E-Model. The results varied across different servers and operators. The highest ping was observed in Singapore (118.77 ms) and ByU (88.61 ms). The most decryption failures were found in Singapore (0.50) and Smartfren (0.32). The highest routing failures were recorded in Hong Kong (0.39) and Smartfren (0.67). The greatest pacer delay occurred in Japan (0.12 ms) and Telkomsel (0.14 ms). In terms of throughput, Japan had the highest value (134.12 Kbps), followed by Smartfren (121.20 Kbps). The highest packet loss rate was observed in Singapore (0.000333%) and ByU (0.00001%). The greatest delay was found in Singapore (19.72 ms) and Telkomsel (19.81 ms), while the highest jitter was recorded in Singapore (19.50 ms) and Telkomsel (20.10 ms). Finally, the MOS results showed that Singapore had the highest score of 3.755 and Telkomsel had a score of 3.750. This comprehensive study provides valuable insights into the performance of 4G network services and Discord voice chat servers in Asia.

articleTitle: Vehicle Driver of Real-time Heart Rate Monitoring with Camera-Based Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: A novel framework has been proposed a remote heart rate (HR) monitoring based on facial recognition and real-time video streaming from a camera. This framework also creates a stable model for long-term HR monitoring and enhances facial identification accuracy while the object is moving. The camera shoots video at a rate of 10 frames per second. Face identification and object tracking are integrated to generate a collection of rectangular faces, which are then sampled in grooves for color changes. The signal related to the HR is represented by the average of the colors inside specified areas of interest (ROI) on faces. HR is derived from differences in face skin color produced by the flow of blood. The feature extraction of signal processing methods such as Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) were used to the color channels in video recordings in order to determine the HR rate derived from the face area. The results show a high level of sensitivity, predictability, accuracy, and mistake detection. The procedure is very exact and consistent.

articleTitle: Close-to-Metal Applications Antenna for IoT: Concise Overview Through Selection Literature
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: Antennas in communication systems are critical components, as well as in the Internet of Things (IoT) system. Demand for antennas that could interconnect in varied environmental conditions is even higher due to increasing use cases of interconnection between one device and another in various industrial and household use. In addition to antennas with metric performances that support high requirement challenges, operating well in environments with metal enclosures or obstacles that sometimes cannot be avoided is also crucial. This article reviews some antenna designs for IoT or other telecommunications system applications, especially with metal enclosures or environmental obstacles. Designing antennas with metal enclosure conditions can be done in several ways considering the use case environment, the required metric performances, and the suitable modification and optimization.

articleTitle: A Verifiable I/O Approach for End-to-end Eligibility Verifiability in Black-box E-Voting Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The tension between upholding verifiability and ensuring voter anonymity is a longstanding obstacle in the development of e-voting systems. Although the concept of “end-to-end verifiability” has been rigorously defined for ballot casting, recording, and tallying, its extension to voter eligibility remains inadequately addressed. To fill this void, we introduce a Black Box model coupled with a verifiable output approach, providing a new lens through which to scrutinize how earlier research has successfully achieved various forms of verifiability. Further, we present a groundbreaking set of principles, named “verifiable eligibility conditions,” which not only evaluate the effectiveness of existing eligibility verification methods but also inspire our streamlined “Verifiable I/O Approach” for achieving end-to-end eligibility verifiability. We conclude by showcasing a comprehensive ticket-based e-voting protocol, offering a tangible implementation of our Verifiable I/O framework.

articleTitle: Application of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT 2) Model to Acceptance of Electronic Learning Media
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: The utilization of online learning media at IDE LPKIA is highly recommended by the institution for its lecturers and students to support teaching and learning activities. SDLR is one of the online learning applications implemented at IDE LPKIA. The success of implementing information technology certainly has its measures. One way to measure the level of success in utilizing information technology is by conducting testing on the technology’s acceptance by users. One of the models used to measure the level of technology acceptance is by applying the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT 2) model. The testing was conducted by distributing questionnaires to students, consisting of 42 statements from the total constructs used. The validity and reliability tests were given to 50 respondents. From the results obtained, all statements were deemed valid and reliable, with the obtained p-values showing Fig.s less than 0.05. The sample used consisted of 205 respondents, for hypothesis testing. The results of the testing stated that effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating condition, hedonic motivation, habit, and user satisfaction have a significant influence on behavior intention, and likewise, behavior intention has a significant influence on use behavior. As for the moderation variables, gender and experience less than 3 years have a significant effect on the relationship between hedonic motivation, facilitating condition, and behavior intention. On the other hand, experience exceeding 3 years has an effect on the relationship between habit and behavior intention.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Crashworthiness Optimization of Crash Box Geometry by Adding Corner Shape Reinforcement Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications (TSSA)
abstract: This research presents a framework for estimating the crashworthiness of a crash box shape using a machine learning approach. The first shape mode used in this study was straight-line reinforcement with two different variant models that are triangle corner and square corner. Curved angle reinforcement was also used as the second shape mode with the convex and concave models as the variations. Both shape modes were compared to the conventional square tube to find out how this optimized structure gives an impact on reducing the peak force during the crash. In order to increase the crashworthiness of crash box shape, structural characteristics were employed as input data. The part machine learning technique’s Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) model was used to predict the energy-absorbing characteristics and the prediction accuracy of different models, which were also utilized as optimization input. The results showed that the convex form generated a lower peak force of 282.1kN when compared to the concave shape, a difference of roughly 7%. As a result, it can be stated that optimizing crash box geometry employing angle reinforcement with a certain design will minimize peak forces for improved crashworthiness.
